description_ru: Жизнь самого знаменитого физика: компас в детстве, работа в бюро в Берне, 1905 год и Нобелевская премия.
text:
Albert Einstein is probably the most famous scientist in history. Many people know his name, his wild grey hair and his kind face. But he was not always a famous man. He was born on March 14, 1879, in the town of Ulm, in Germany. His father, Hermann, had a small business, and his mother, Pauline, played the piano very well. When Albert was one year old, the family moved to the big city of Munich.

Albert was a quiet and thoughtful child. Some people say he started to talk late, and he did not like noisy games with other boys. When he was five, he was ill in bed, and his father gave him a small compass. Albert watched the needle for a long time. It always pointed north, and nobody touched it! He thought, "Something invisible makes it move." That day he started to ask questions about the world, and he never stopped.

His mother taught him to play the violin when he was six. At first he did not like it, but later he loved music very much. He played the violin all his life, and he often said that music helped him to think. He also read many books about science and maths. At twelve he got a book about geometry, and he called it his holy little book. He learned everything in it in one summer.

School was not easy for Albert. He did not like his strict teachers in Germany, because they wanted students to repeat words, not to think. At sixteen he went to Switzerland and wanted to enter a university in Zurich. He was younger than the other students, and he did not pass the first exam. But his maths and physics marks were excellent. He studied for a year at a school in a small town, and then he entered the university.

After university Albert could not find a good job as a teacher. In 1902 he started to work in an office in Bern, in Switzerland. His job was to look at the ideas of other people and decide if they were good. The work was easy, so he had a lot of free time. He often hid his own papers in a drawer and worked on them in the office. In 1903 he married Mileva Maric, a friend from university. They had two sons.

The year 1905 was the most amazing year in his life. In only one year, this young man in a small office wrote four important papers. They changed physics for ever. In one paper he showed that light is made of tiny pieces. In another one he talked about time and space, and he said that time is not the same for everybody. He also wrote a famous short idea about energy, E equals m c squared. Many people could not understand it, but it was true.

Soon the world listened to him. Albert became a professor and worked in several cities. In 1915 he finished his big idea about gravity. In 1919 scientists watched the sun during an eclipse, and they saw that his idea was right. The next morning newspapers around the world wrote about Einstein. In 1921 he won the Nobel Prize in Physics. People loved him. They came to hear him speak, and they shouted his name in the street.

In 1933 life in Germany became dangerous, because Adolf Hitler was now the leader, and Albert was Jewish. He left Europe and went to the United States. He lived in a quiet town called Princeton and worked at a university there. He also liked to sail his small boat on a lake, and he was not a very good sailor! He walked to work every day, and children often stopped him to ask about their homework. He always helped them.

Albert was a gentle man, and he cared about peace. He did not like wars, and he spoke about this many times. In 1952 Israel asked him to be its president, but he said no. He said that he knew science better than people. He liked simple things: old clothes, long walks and a pipe, and he often did not wear socks. He died on April 18, 1955, at the age of seventy-six. Today we still use his ideas in many things, for example in satellites and in the maps on our phones. His curious mind is a good example for all of us.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Кончик языка между зубами, струя воздуха без голоса; не «с» и не «ф».
Скольжение от «а» к «и»; второй элемент короткий.
Долгий звук между «ё» и «э», губы не округляйте.
Спинка языка к нёбу, звук идёт через нос; не добавляйте «г» в конце.

questions.question: What did Albert's father give him when he was five?
questions.answer: He gave him a small compass.

questions.question: What instrument did Albert play all his life?
Where did Albert work in 1902?
questions.answer: He worked in an office in Bern, in Switzerland.

questions.question: Why did Albert go to the United States?
questions.answer: Life in Germany became dangerous, because Hitler was the leader and Albert was Jewish.
